summary: Noninteractive CI service account denied cross-account access due to org-policy tag scoping
description: Issue summary: Noninteractive CI pipeline (build/infra-deploy) started failing to access cross-account S3 and KMS resources after the org-policy tag enforcement rollout on 2026-03-09. Impact: Blocking scheduled releases and automated infra changes for multiple teams. Scope: Affects pipelines using GCP Workload Identity Federation -> AWS assume-role flow (noninteractive service accounts).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger CI job 'infra-deploy-prod' using noninteractive service account sa-ci-builder@redwood-prod. 2) Job attempts to federate via GCP WIF to assume roles in aws-prod-account. 3) AWS STS AssumeRole is rejected with AccessDenied logged from org-policy evaluation. 4) Observe error in pipeline logs and AWS CloudTrail 'Denied' event with condition mismatch.
error_logs: Pipeline error snippet: 'AccessDenied: The request was denied by an organization policy condition: TagConditionMismatch (Required tag: env=prod; provided tags: env=prod,team=infra,build_id=20260310-very-long-id)'. CloudTrail event: 'AssumeRoleDenied - sts:Tagging not permitted: session tags contain attribute 'build_id' with length 36 which exceeds org policy max-length=24'.
investigation_notes: Timeline: - 2026-03-09 02:00: Org-policy tag-length enforcement rollout (internal change) applied to aws-prod-account. - 2026-03-10 08:12: First CI failure observed for infra-deploy pipeline. - Verified role trust policy and WIF provider are unchanged. - Confirmed that interactive user flows (console sessions) are allowed because they don't pass the same set of session tags. Hypothesis: Noninteractive CI includes a build_id session tag with a long value; org-policy tag-length/whitelist now denies the AssumeRole request. Additional observation: the federated role session name is being url-encoded by the WIF shim which increases the session tag payload; tags are being validated against organization SCP/TagPolicy before role is assumed. Reproduced locally by calling sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity with a crafted token and long tag; AWS returns same denial code.
mitigation_workaround: Short-term workaround implemented at 2026-03-10 14:30: - CI team updated pipeline to strip 'build_id' session tag for production assume-role flow (patch applied to pipeline shim). - Re-ran blocked jobs; jobs succeeded after tag removal. Note: This is a mitigation, not a policy change.
root_cause_summary: Org-policy tag validation enforcement was rolled out without compatible tag-normalization rules for noninteractive federated sessions. Noninteractive CI sends a high-cardinality, long-form 'build_id' session tag which violations the new tag-length constraints. AWS rejects the AssumeRole attempt during org-policy evaluation, causing access denied for the CI service account.
permanent_fix_plan: 1) Update CI federation shim to normalize and truncate session tags to the org-policy allowed schema; add a whitelist of safe tags. 2) Coordinate with Cloud Security to publish allowed tag keys/lengths and include examples for noninteractive flows. 3) Add integration tests in CI for WIF->STS assume-role flows against a staging policy before org-policy rollouts. 4) Consider automated rollback guard for tag-policy changes that detect impact on noninteractive principals.
next_steps: - (Assigned) Diego Ramos: Implement tag normalization in CI shim and open PR by 2026-03-12. - (Action) Cloud Security: Publish allowed tag key/length matrix and notify affected teams by 2026-03-12. - (Action) SRE: Add a smoke test for federated assume-role in the pre-deploy policy gating pipeline by 2026-03-18.
